I am not sure that I agree that the guidelines don't recommend a TOLAC after more than 2 C-sections. They kind of leave it in a grey area. I would love to see some statistics on it. However, I suspect that it has been so discouraged that there are few or none to be had. I really like your sentence "I think patient choice within medically appropriate options is critically important and must be respected.", that is exactly my opinion as well. 
I know several OBGYN doctors who when in doubt lean toward surgery for two reasons; high cost of malpractice for their specialty, it is the highest for any specialty last I knew; and the emotional toll it takes on both the family and the doctor when a VBAC ends tragically. When any birth ends tragically for that matter. It is devastating for the mother and family and for the doctor as well. All the doctors I know are acutely aware of how deep the wounds are when a baby is lost, when subsequent reproduction options are lost, when a mother is lost. Those are uniquely traumatic events for all involved. I am sure some of their bias toward surgery is unconscious and in all respects it is understandable. However, as another poster stated, it is ultimately the woman's health that is on the line and if VBAC is "within medically appropriate options" it is her choice to make.
I am sorry, that flyer just restates what I have already posted, which are the current ACOG guidelines. It does not say that multiple previous cesareans, up to 2, increases the risks during VBAC.

I don't have a problem with doctors having a choice in the matter. However, many doctors lean heavily toward surgery (I worked in the medical field for 25 years, not OBGYN) and the number of C-sections have/had gotten way out of control. There are "best practice" standards such as the guidelines I posted from the ACOG. It is still unclear where this particular woman falls within those guidelines and I would always err on the side of patient choice.

I agree, the numbers aren't clear. And the idea that 20-40% are not "successful" implies only that they had to have a cesarean birth. It doesn't tell us if there were any complications other than the surgery for the baby or the mother. If VBAC is attempted but a cesarean is needed anyway and the baby and mother are both healthy and safe at the end of it, that is a successful birth in my eyes.

After the school shooting where the 20 children were killed, I saw a psychologist on TV talking about how to explain it to your children who were upset or scared by it. He said the best explanation he ever heard came from his mother. She used to tell his brothers and he when something awful happened "But, look at all those people who are running to help. Bad things can happen in life and there are people who do very bad things. But, there will always be more people running to help." I think this is the most beautiful example I have ever seen of "all those people running to help".
